subhead: Take a free practice quiz or point your phone at any General Chemistry exam question for an instant, explained answer — stoichiometry and bonding without the guesswork.
metaTitle: General Chemistry Practice Quiz & Questions | Cambo
metaDescription: Free General Chemistry I quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Atomic structure, stoichiometry, periodic trends, and chemical bonding.
whyItWorks: General Chemistry questions often hinge on a specific calculation — balancing an equation, converting moles to grams, finding a limiting reactant — where one arithmetic or conceptual slip changes the final answer. Cambo reads the exact problem, including any structure or equation shown, and walks through the calculation step by step.

sampleQuestions.q: An atom has 17 protons, 18 neutrons, and 17 electrons. What is its mass number?
sampleQuestions.a: 35 — the mass number is the sum of protons and neutrons (17 + 18 = 35); electrons don't count toward mass number since their mass is negligible.

sampleQuestions.q: Which type of bond forms when electrons are transferred from one atom to another, such as between sodium and chlorine?
sampleQuestions.a: An ionic bond — it forms through the transfer of one or more electrons from a metal (like sodium) to a nonmetal (like chlorine), creating oppositely charged ions that attract each other.

sampleQuestions.q: In the balanced equation 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O, how many moles of water are produced from 5 moles of O2, assuming excess H2?
sampleQuestions.a: 10 moles — the balanced equation shows a 1:2 mole ratio between O2 and H2O, so 5 moles of O2 produces 5 x 2 = 10 moles of water.

sampleQuestions.q: As you move left to right across a period on the periodic table, atomic radius generally:
options: Increases, because more electron shells are added
Decreases, because increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons in the same shell closer
Stays the same across a period
sampleQuestions.a: Atomic radius generally decreases across a period, because protons are added to the nucleus without adding a new electron shell, so the increasing positive charge pulls the existing electrons in more tightly.

sampleQuestions.q: A reaction combines 2 mol of A with 3 mol of B according to the equation A + 2B → C. Which reactant is the limiting reactant?
options: A, because it has fewer moles
B, because 2 mol of A would require 4 mol of B, but only 3 mol of B is available
Neither — they are both fully consumed
C, because it is the product
sampleQuestions.a: B is the limiting reactant — the equation requires 2 moles of B for every mole of A, so 2 mol of A needs 4 mol of B, but only 3 mol of B is on hand, meaning B runs out first.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the electron configuration notation for a neutral oxygen atom (atomic number 8)?
sampleQuestions.a: 1s2 2s2 2p4 — with 8 total electrons, the first two fill the 1s orbital, the next two fill the 2s orbital, and the remaining four go into the 2p orbitals.

faqs.q: What topics does General Chemistry I usually cover?
faqs.a: Atomic structure and electron configuration, periodic trends, chemical bonding (ionic, covalent, and metallic), stoichiometry and balancing equations, states of matter, and an introduction to solutions and gas laws.

faqs.q: Does General Chemistry I usually include a lab component?
faqs.a: Yes — most schools pair the lecture with a required lab section, often as its own 1-credit-hour course, since hands-on lab work is typically part of the science gen-ed requirement it fulfills.

faqs.q: Do I need a strong math background for General Chemistry?
faqs.a: Basic algebra is generally sufficient for General Chemistry I — you'll do a lot of unit conversions and mole calculations, but calculus isn't usually required until later chemistry or physics coursework.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with McGraw Hill, Pearson, Cengage, or any university?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool and isn't produced, endorsed, or affiliated with any textbook publisher or university.

faqs.q: Is General Chemistry I usually curved?
faqs.a: It's common for large-lecture General Chemistry sections to curve exams, since problem-set-style tests can produce a wide spread of scores, but this varies by instructor and department.

faqs.q: How many credit hours is General Chemistry I usually worth?
faqs.a: Typically 3-4 credit hours for lecture, often with an additional 1 credit hour for the paired lab section.
